M4C Outcome 2: Improved socio-economic security for women market vendors. Capacity Development for Rural Women Market Vendors 2022 (Kadavu) • 178 rural farmers (89 rural women, 25 youth, 65 men) have increased business and financial skills, such as starting and maintaining savings and recording-keeping. • 30 rural women market vendors develop digital literacy, using online platforms to strengthen their business, like marketing their produce or strengthening and maintaining their network via social media platforms. • 65 rural women accessed gender – inclusive financial and social services • 75 rural women market vendors have increased economic and sustainable livelihoods through improved climate change resilient agricultural practices, and value-adding activities. • 65 rural women market vendors (including 15 couples, and 15 youths) have increased economic and sustainable livelihoods through improved climate change resilient agricultural practices, and value-adding activities. • 65 rural women market vendors have contributed knowledge sharing on agricultural pest and disease, soil care and plant nutrients, with options to preserve salted meat, pawpaw pickle, vegetable pickle, tomato chutney, fruit jams. Tools and Seeds Distribution 2022: • In Kadavu, 300 farmers improved farming practices due to the support on distribution of tools, seeds, wheelbarrows, raincoats, and protective equipment’s (300 households – couple, youth, people living with disability – inclusive approach). Partnership Meetings 2022: • Strengthened partnership between government partners based in Vunisea, Kadavu. This includes I-Taukei Affairs, and Provincial Administrator • Ten financial institutions participated in market business fair, resulting in strengthened service delivery to rural communities. • M4C Project staff participated in sub-committee meetings of financial institutions at the Reserve Bank of Fiji Monitoring 2022: • 150 rural women market vendors have demonstrated some level of improvement in socioeconomic security • 45 rural women demonstrated agency in financial decision-making in their business and households. • 25 rural women, 10 youths, and 20 couples were able to access gender-inclusive financial and social services. • 45 rural women, 20 men and 10 youths are able to increase business and financial skills, such as starting and maintain savings and recording-keeping. • 10 rural women market vendors accessed digital literacy, using online platforms to strengthen their business, like marketing their produce or strengthening and maintaining their network via social media platforms. • 150 rural women market vendors have increased economic and sustainable livelihoods through improved climate change resilient agricultural practices, and value-adding activities. • 25 rural women have improved access to health, safety, and other social services.
Samoa • Approximately 1400 vendors (900 females & 500 males) benefitted directly from the distribution of Covid supplies (disposal facemasks, sanitizers, etc. to Fugalei and Salelologa Markets)
• Partnership with Ministry of Industry and Labor resulted in potential marketing and branding training opportunities for upskilling market vendors.

The target was not achieved due to the Covid 19 restrictions. However, later in December , 145 market vendor farmers were supported with the handing over of Projectors, Pull Up Screen and hard drive as part of online learnings. In addition, the farmers in Kadavu were supported with disposable masks, hand sanitizers and micro insurance awareness information sheets. The awareness programme was conducted in three districts ( Sanima, Naceva and Tavuki) in Kadavu. Consultation meeting was conducted with key partners in Kadavu, to discuss the upcoming activities planned for Kadavu.
